primitives.name: Bayesian Random Effects Model
primitives.verbatim_quote: In stage one of our model, we fit a Bayesian mixed-effects model on log expected goals per minute with team and opponent random effects estimated separately for even-strength, power-play, and penalty-kill phases and home/away settings.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'xG_ij': 'Expected goals for game i, team j (dimensionless)', 'mu_team_i': 'Random intercept for home team i (dimensionless)', 'mu_opponent_j': 'Random intercept for away team j (dimensionless)', 'mu_phase_k': 'Fixed effect for phase k (strengths/power play/penalty kill/home advantage) (dimensionless)', 'sigma_squared': 'Variance of residual noise (dimensionless)', 'home': 'Binary indicator for home game (dimensionless)'}
primitives.assumptions: Team and opponent effects are normally distributed random variables, conditional independence of goals given covariates, and linear additivity of fixed and random effects.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Fails when team sample size is too small, leading to over-shrinkage toward global mean; also breaks down if there are extreme outliers in shot quality.

layer2.mapping: GSI: Posterior predictive checks for bookmaker efficiency. GSE: State-transition kernel for updating team skill matrices.
layer2.telemetry: Effective sample size diagnostics (R-hat < 1.05) and posterior predictive checks on holdout data.

primitives.name: Monte Carlo Simulation
primitives.verbatim_quote: This data was then run through 30,000 Monte Carlo simulations per matchup to produce our win probabilities.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'N': 'Number of simulations (N = 30,000) (dimensionless)', 'win_prob': 'Probability of winning a single simulation (dimensionless)', 'lambda': 'Poisson rate parameter for goals in a phase (goals per minute)', 't': 'Duration of a phase (minutes)'}
primitives.assumptions: Goals follow independent Poisson processes with rate $\lambda$, and overtime follows a geometric distribution for sudden death.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down under dependent goal scoring (e.g., special teams powerplay goals) and if underlying distributions are misspecified.

layer2.mapping: GSI: Synthetic data generation for robustness testing. GSE: Policy optimization via trajectory sampling.
layer2.telemetry: Convergence diagnostics on win-probability estimates (standard error < 0.3%) and consistency across multiple runs.

primitives.name: Expected Goals Conversion
primitives.verbatim_quote: These estimates were back-transformed and converted into true expected goal differential per 60 for each phase, weighted by the distribution of each team's actual ice time in each phase and converted to composite zscores.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'xG_diff_phase': 'Expected goal differential per 60 minutes for a given phase (goals per 60 min)', 'beta_hat_team': 'Posterior mean estimate of team effect (dimensionless)', 'beta_hat_opponent': 'Posterior mean estimate of opponent effect (dimensionless)'}
primitives.assumptions: Exponential transformation stabilizes variance, and log-ratio scale is appropriate for multiplicative effects.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Fails when team ice-time distributions are highly skewed, causing misallocation of strength estimates.

layer2.mapping: GSI: Rank-based transformations for fair comparison across leagues. GSE: Value function approximation via state-action pairs.
layer2.telemetry: Ice-time balance diagnostics and correlation between transformed z-scores and observed goal differentials.

primitives.name: Offensive Line Disparity Ratio
primitives.verbatim_quote: We also studied how offensive line disparity impacts team performance by isolating the first offensive line's and second offensive line's performances and creating a ratio.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'xG_for_O1': 'Expected goals for scored by first offensive line (goals)', 'xG_for_O2': 'Expected goals for scored by second offensive line (goals)', 'Disparity_Ratio': 'Dimensionless ratio measuring relative offensive output'}
primitives.assumptions: Shot quality is consistent across lines, and the ratio captures meaningful variation in offensive workload distribution.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down if line usage is confounded with matchup quality or if small sample sizes lead to noisy estimates.

layer2.mapping: GSI: Heterogeneous treatment effect estimation for lineup strategies. GSE: Multi-agent reinforcement learning for line pairing optimization.
layer2.telemetry: Correlation between disparity ratio and final standings position, controlling for overall team strength.

Our pipeline addresses two core failures: ignoring opponent quality and treating goals as exchangeable. By placing a hierarchical prior on team effects, shrinkage pulls weak estimates toward the mean, reducing variance inflation from playing weaker schedules. The Monte Carlo approach propagates uncertainty from the posterior into outcome projections, yielding robust win probabilities. Crucially, this framework allows us to isolate specific aspects of team performance (like line disparity) while adjusting for confounding factors.
